18.30.3.en: When both the mind that loves God and the soul come to understanding, then it (the body) is easily tamed even against its will, and the soul by means of the mind can quench every animal movement [35].

18.30.4.en: v Those who are not content with sufficiency, but seek more (with lust), enslave themselves to the passions that disturb and bring into them all evil thoughts and apprehensions, that is, all that is evil, although we need to obtain new good things. And just as garments that are excessively long hinder travelers from walking, so excessive desire for possessions hinders the soul from striving and being saved [36].

18.30.5.en: St. Anthony the Great St. Augustine addresses the Lord in prayer, asking for the work of grace in him, since by his own personal abilities he cannot be freed from passions and lusts; so in his Confessions he declares his need for God's work in him, that He may fulfill what He commands him.

18.30.6.en: v I heard a divine voice commanding me: "Take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness" (Lk 21:34). Wine is far from me; have mercy on me lest drunkenness come near me.

18.30.7.en: In any case gluttony sometimes tries to creep in to seize Your servant. Have mercy on me, that it may depart from me! For no one can be chaste unless You give it to him (Wis 8:21).

18.30.8.en: You give us much when we pray. And all that we have received of good things even before prayer, we received from You. And the truth we learned lately is that we received it from You.

18.30.9.en: I was never a drunkard, but I know many drunkards who through You became exceedingly lofty men. For it is Your work that these, who were never thus and who ought not to have been thus, have become thus. They are Your works, that they may learn from Him who worked in them thus.

18.30.10.en: I have also heard another statement from You: "Do not follow your passions, but restrain your lusts" (see Sir 18:29).

18.30.11.en: Through Your help I heard another statement that I loved very much: "For neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse" (1 Cor 8:8). In other words, the first does not make me rich, nor the last poor.

18.30.12.en: I also heard another statement: "I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content... both to abound and to suffer need.

18.30.13.en: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me" (Phil 4:11-13)... He strengthens me so that I am able to do that. Grant me, You who commanded, and command what You will.

18.30.14.en: This man (St. Paul) confessed that he had received this, therefore he glories in the Lord (1 Cor 1:31).

18.30.15.en: I heard another man pray in order to receive, saying: "Remove from me the gluttony of the belly" (see Sir 23:6). It is clear from this, O holy God, that You are the one who gives, and that You do what You have commanded to be done [37].

18.30.16.en: v It befits man to be spiritual in order to keep the Law spiritually; this is not through the Law but by grace, that is, not through the commandment but through the free gift, not through the impulse of the letter but the impulse of the Spirit. Now man begins to be renewed inwardly according to grace, on condition that he does not follow what he loves in his mind, nor agree with what the flesh presses upon him and which he hates. This does not mean that he is entirely free of evil lusts, but that he does not follow them (18:30) [38].

18.30.17.en: v Obeying the commandment "Thou shalt not covet" (Ex 20:17) is one thing, and trying to refrain from practicing it is another. Where man follows what is written: "Do not follow your desire".

18.30.18.en: And so that you may know that without the grace of the Savior no one can carry out the first commandment or the other. In order to practice righteousness in the true worship of God, fight in an inner struggle against the inner evil of lust, and to attain perfect righteousness by there being no adversary at all. For whoever fights is always exposed to danger, and sometimes is wounded even if he does not fall. But he who has no enemy enjoys complete peace.

18.30.19.en: And it is rightly said that he is without sin in whom sin does not live. Nor does the one who refrains from evil works declare: "For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do" (Rom 7:20) [39].

18.30.20.en: v What is the accomplishment of goodness but ceasing from evil and ending it? And what is ceasing from evil but what the Law says: "Thou shalt not covet" (Rom 7:7; Ex 20:17)? Coveting is not the fulfilling of goodness, for it is the finishing of evil... Therefore he says: "But how to perform that which is good I find not" (Rom 7:18).

18.30.21.en: I am unable to accomplish what is said: "Thou shalt not covet." What then do I need? To accomplish: "Do not follow your passions" (Sir 18:29). Do this as long as unlawful lusts are present in your body... Do not give yourself over to your lusts, for if you follow them you give them strength. And by giving them strength, how will you triumph over your enemies when you support them against yourself by your strength? Then what is perfect freedom in the Lord Jesus, who said: "If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed"? When does perfect freedom exist? When there are no enemies, and when "the last enemy that shall be destroyed is death" (1 Cor 15:26)...

18.30.22.en: Let us, the wounded, beseech the Physician, that we may be carried to the inn so that we may be healed [by the Good Shepherd (Lk 10:30-35)]. It is He who promises health, who has compassion on the man left half dead on the road by the robbers [40].

18.30.23.en: St. Augustine Father Fulgentius, the disciple of St. Augustine, links this statement with the saying of the Lord Christ: "He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal. If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be" (Jn 12:25-26).

18.30.24.en: v How does he who loves his life lose it? He does this who follows his obstinate passions, he who pleases them more than he should. Therefore the Holy Bible warns us in the words: "Do not follow your passions" (Sir 18:29). If you follow them you lose yourself, for this behavior is off the road that leads to virtue. That is like the opposite behavior: he who hates it in this world saves it... Truly, unless you die you bear no fruit for yourself [41].

18.30.25.en: Father Fulgentius v Pleasant is the present life and full of many pleasures, but not for all, only for those who are drawn to it. If someone looks to heaven and sees the beautiful things there, at once he disdains this life and does not care for it. Just as the beauty of anything is admired when nothing more beautiful is seen, but when something better appears the former is disdained. Therefore if we choose to look to that beauty, and observe the loftiness of the Kingdom there, we free ourselves from the present bonds, for sympathy with things, as Christ says, brings us to this: "He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal; if any man serve me, let him follow me" (Jn 12:25-26).

18.30.26.en: The words seem like a riddle, but they are not, but are full of great wisdom. But how: he who loves his life loses it? When he practices its improper lusts, when he satisfies his lusts where it was necessary to do otherwise. Thus one advises us: "Do not follow your desire" (see Sir 29:18) [42].

18.30.27.en: St. John Chrysostom If you fill your soul with lust in pleasure, it makes you a mockery of your enemies [30].

18.30.28.en: v Not only is this self-control worthy of praise in moderation in food, but also moderation in lust. For it is written: "Do not follow your passions, but restrain your lusts, for if you allow yourself satisfaction in lust, it will make you a laughingstock to your enemies" (see Sir 18:29-30). And he says afterward: "Wine and women lead the wise astray" (see Sir 19:2). Paul teaches us moderation in marriage itself, so whoever is not chaste in marriage, this is counted a kind of adultery, and breaks the law of the Apostle [43].

18.30.29.en: St. Ambrose v Man, though he is ahead of all these (creatures) in dignity, did not understand and ignored following God and the desire to be like his Creator, and became a slave to the lusts of the body. "He is compared to the dull beasts and has become like them."

18.30.30.en: At one time he resembles a lustful horse, neighing after his companion's wife (Jer 5:8).

18.30.31.en: And at another time like a ravening wolf, lying in wait for strangers (Ezek 22:27).

18.30.32.en: And at another time, because of his deceiving his brother, he makes himself a base fox (Ezek 13:4).

18.30.33.en: Truly there is increasing folly, for he who was created in the image of the Creator is likened to the beast that has no reason. He does not know his structure from the beginning, nor desires to understand the great dispensations made for his sake; at least to learn his dignity from them, but he does not care for the truth, casting off from himself the image of the heavenly to take the image of the earthly. And that he might not remain in sin, for his sake "the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us" (Jn 1:14), and "emptied Himself and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross" (Phil 2:8).

18.30.34.en: If you do not care for your first origin, then for the sake of the price that was paid for you accept at least some thought of your dignity, and look to what was offered in your place, and be assured of what you have been qualified for. You were bought with the precious blood of Christ, so do not be slaves to sin. Understand your dignity, and do not be like the dull beasts.

18.30.35.en: "This their way is a stumbling block to them" (Ps 48:13) LXX. God who manages our affairs hinders us from walking in evil, so He places obstacles and hindrances that we may shrink from the unreasoning life, after which we rejoice with our tongue. With the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession of faith is made unto our salvation (see Rom 10:10). Paul persecuted the Church of Christ; he despoiled it, and pressed on his part with evil (Acts 8:3), and afterward he rejoiced in his understanding, declaring to the synagogue that this is the Christ (Acts 9:22) [44].

18.30.36.en: St. Basil the Great v "Like sheep they are driven to the abyss; death shall feed on them" (Ps 49:14).

18.30.37.en: This is he who leads into captivity those who resemble the beasts, and are compared to the dull flocks like sheep, which have no reason nor ability to defend themselves, and he is the enemy who brought them down to his prison, and delivered them to death to shepherd them. For death reigned over them from the days of Adam until the leadership of Moses (Rom 5:14), until the true Shepherd came and laid down His life for His flock, and raised them together and led them (Jn 10:3-18) from the prison of the abyss to the dawn of the resurrection, and delivered them to the righteous, that is, to His angels, to shepherd them.

18.30.38.en: "And the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning." Every believer is accompanied by an angel worthy to look upon the Father in heaven. These upright ones, then, have dominion over them when they are freed from the harshest bitter bondage, and have dominion over them in the morning, that is, when they advance in the rising of the light.

18.30.39.en: Consider all the groups of words written. When man was in dignity he did not understand, he became like the dull beasts. He who has dignity, and did not know himself because of the sin dwelling in him, became like the dull beasts. Therefore, since he became estranged from the Word of God and became a dumb beast, the enemy drove him like an unattended flock, and cast him into the abyss, and delivered him to death to shepherd him.

18.30.40.en: Therefore when he is saved from this, and freed from the evil shepherd (death), he says: "The Lord is my shepherd" (Ps 23:1). It is no longer death but life, and instead of falling there is resurrection, and instead of deception there is truth.

18.30.41.en: [And their help shall wear away in the abyss] (Ps 49:14) LXX. Perhaps he speaks here of death, for with all its help it cannot preserve those it shepherded, this one whom (Christ) who has authority over death destroys (Heb 2:14), for all their help is old and weak. At that time the help of those who were deceived in mind, and were proud because of wealth or glory or power, appears vain.

18.30.42.en: "Shall wear away in the abyss" as their weakness is realized. Or perhaps the help of the righteous who were saved by the Lord dissolves in the abyss, since they have not yet received the promises, for God has provided some better thing for us, that those who preceded us "without us should not be made perfect" (Heb 11:40).

18.30.43.en: "But God will redeem my soul from the hand of the abyss, for He will receive me" (Ps 49:15) LXX. It is clear that he prophesies of the descent of the Lord into hell, who saves the soul of the prophet with others, and he does not remain there [45].

18.30.44.en: St. Basil the Great Do not enjoy excessive luxury, so that you do not bind yourself to its expenses [31].

18.30.45.en: v What are we to do about this fact, that the Apostle himself gave us a huge list of vices, and pointed out among them drunkenness and concluded it with a warning not to eat bread with those who sin in such things? [46]

18.30.46.en: v It is a matter that arouses pity, reminding us how serious it is to eat with those who sin by gluttony even in their homes [47].

18.30.47.en: St. Augustine Do not become a beggar by holding banquets and do not borrow money, when there is nothing in your purse [33].

18.30.48.en: Regarding gluttony or greed or the lust of the belly, many of the Fathers, especially the ascetics, count the taming of the lust of the belly as giving victory over all thoughts and temptations. St. Mar Philoxenus, Bishop of Mabbug, devoted, in his Memre, thirteen discourses to speaking of gluttony. In them he highlighted that the lust of the belly is the most defiling of the passions, deprives us of prudent thought, and is the door of all evils, enslaves the soul as well as the body, and hinders tenderness, and being against fasting it destroys prayer and causes sluggishness [48].

18.30.49.en: St. Mar Philoxenus distinguishes between hunger and the lust of the belly: hunger is a gift from the Creator that supports health without falling into the lust of the belly, which destroys man's authority and enslaves him to other lusts. God created man a god over his belly, feeding it and not being enslaved to it.

18.30.50.en: St. Mar Philoxenus presents to us the problem of the lust of the belly through three serious examples: Adam in his simplicity through the lust of the belly (Gen 3:6), and Esau lost his birthright and its blessings for the same reason (Gen 25:34), and the people of Israel through the lust of the belly worshiped the golden calf and forgot God (Ex 32:19).

18.30.51.en: The following are some excerpts from this discourse:

18.30.52.en: v The person who submits to this base lust cannot accept the yoke of discipleship to Christ... As soon as the stomach becomes master over the body, it commands and subdues all its will, and instead of the road ascending to heaven, it shows him the other road that descends to the abyss [49].

18.30.53.en: v This lust of the belly is baser than all the passions. As soon as a person becomes its servant and carries its yoke on his shoulders, it no longer allows him rest from serving it. He serves it night and day, and it sends him everywhere it desires like an exhausted servant, not on a clean road but on roads full of stumbling blocks, and to a place where there are harmful things, a lover of the lust of things who has no eyes that see the light, because even if he wishes it, the weight of food makes them grow dark. The day for him is night, and the night is double death [50].

18.30.54.en: v God created the animals for two things: while all that belongs to their life is eating, they also do a service for the human race, but the gluttonous man eats and does not work. While he is zealous for the table, he is stripped of all important works. The soul that serves the belly does not perceive God, for it is dead to all thoughts of knowledge, and to contemplation of God, since the knowledge of the soul proceeds from the illumination of the body and the members of the body. And the illumination of the body proceeds from reducing food, but surely the gluttonous man is burdened with two yokes, namely the darkness of thoughts and the weight of the body [51]

18.30.55.en: St. Mar Philoxenus Inspired by Sirach 18

18.31.s.en: I praise You, O great Creator, for Your dispensation!

18.31.0.en: v Allow Your earthly creation to emulate the heavenly creation, O my wonderful Creator!

18.31.1.en: I stand with the whole universe, as in a chorus unable to express Your wonderful dispensation!

18.31.2.en: You provide the earthly body with its needs, so it is satisfied and quenched, and for my soul love and tenderness and joy and immortality.

18.31.3.en: You embrace me with Your care, so I lack nothing.

18.31.4.en: v My sin brought me down to deprivation of life; the abyss opened its mouth to swallow me and there was no rescuer.

18.31.5.en: You came down to earth, and became incarnate that I might draw near to You.

18.31.6.en: You accepted death, that by Your resurrection I might tread on death under my feet!

18.31.7.en: You accepted the wounds in Your body, so You clothed it with glory instead of disgrace and shame.

18.31.8.en: The crown of thorns was placed on Your head, and it blossomed and offered me heavenly roses.

18.31.9.en: Your side was pierced with the spear and poured out blood and water. By Your blood You cleansed me, O Righteous One, from my sins, and by the water You gave me, by Your Holy Spirit, the spirit of adoption.

18.31.10.en: Whenever I look to the dispensation of Your salvation I stand in bewilderment; who can describe Your love and Your mercies?!

18.31.11.en: You offered me complete pardon, and clothed me with the garment of Your righteousness.

18.31.12.en: Even if my days reach a thousand years, they are like a drop of water from the sea of eternity, and a grain of sand in the desert.

18.31.13.en: You revealed to me Your longsuffering and the overflowing of Your mercy!

18.31.14.en: v In Your love for all mankind You rebuke and discipline and train and teach, and bring back the lost sheep not to the Garden of Eden but to Paradise, to join them to the chorus of the heavenly ones.

18.31.15.en: v Your kindness to men is indescribable, and Your giving is beyond estimation.

18.31.16.en: Grant us kindness, that we may offer our brothers of what You have given us:

18.31.17.en: The sweet word with spiritual and psychological and material gifts.

18.31.18.en: Whatever we offer, we draw from the storehouses of Your love that we may be enriched and offer to our brothers.

18.31.19.en: Grant us Your longsuffering, that we may judge no one before the time.

18.31.20.en: Grant us of Your humility, that however much honor we offer our brothers, we shall not reach the last row which was reserved for You alone, O You who were crucified for us!

18.31.21.en: v Your being lifted up on the cross is the only remedy to heal the diseases of my soul.

18.31.22.en: For my sake You sanctified Yourself, You who are Holy, and as a member of Your body I vow my life to You, desiring that all mankind be sanctified with me.

18.31.23.en: Gladden my heart by my returning to You with all mankind.

18.31.24.en: Let us hear Your wonderful voice:

18.31.25.en: Today you shall be with Me in Paradise.

18.31.26.en: Let my heart ascend to it now, and I will not postpone even for a moment.

18.31.27.en: Truly from morning to evening the time changes.

18.31.28.en: You have shone upon me, O Sun of Righteousness, so I do not wait until evening, but throw myself into Your embrace, and cry out with Jacob my father: "I will not let thee go, except thou bless me" (Gen 32:26)!

18.31.29.en: v Accompany me, that I may enjoy Your divine presence all the moments of my life.

18.31.30.en: I do not follow my passions, for Your love sanctifies me.

18.31.31.en: Who restrains my lusts, except the desire to enjoy union with You?!

18.31.32.en: I no longer suffer from gluttony, for the bread of this world does not give life.

18.31.33.en: I do not spend on the pleasures and tables of the world, for my heart and my thought and my senses and my emotions and all my energies are completely absorbed in Your love!
